items.title: pip-rns docs
items.text:
These guides explain how to install packages over Reticulum and how to move wheels offline with opip.

You choose every source. Nothing ships with a vendor index. Indexes and aliases are opt-in.

items.title: Tools
items.text: Tool Role pip-rns / pipx-rns Install from rngit remotes with pip, pipx, uv, or poetry opip Build, verify, and install offline .opip bundles

items.title: Read in order
items.text:
1. Getting started - install the tools and run a first command
  2. pip-rns - remotes, releases, backends, and day-to-day installs
  3. opip - create and install integrity-backed wheel bundles
  4. Trust and signing - publishers, verification, and fail-closed behavior
  5. Discovery - browse, discover, search, aliases, and indexes
  6. Sneakernet - USB and air-gap paths end to end
  7. Troubleshooting - doctor, PEP 668, and common fixes

items.title: Quick picks
items.text:
Want a package from the mesh right now?

pip-rns browse --install

Need to hand someone a USB stick?

opip create -r requirements.txt -o ./pkg.opip
opip export ./pkg.opip -o /media/usb/pkg.opip

On the other machine:

opip verify /media/usb/pkg.opip --require-signature
opip install /media/usb/pkg.opip

items.title: Also available
items.text:
• Site: https://pip-rns.quad4.io/
  • Source and compact reference: https://github.com/Quad4-Software/pip-rns
  • pip-rns help and opip help (add -i for a menu)
  • Man pages under man/man1/

items.title: Discovery
items.text:
When remotes announce on Reticulum, you can listen, scan for Python packages, search by short name, and install without typing full rns:// paths.

Resolution order for a short name:

  1. Local aliases
  2. Synced indexes you registered
  3. Packages found by discovery scan

Nothing is pre-selected. You only see nodes that announce while you listen, and indexes you add yourself.

items.title: Browse (one command)
items.text:
Listen, save, scan, optionally alias, and install:

pip-rns browse --install

Useful flags:

pip-rns browse --seconds 60 --auto-alias
pip-rns browse --no-listen --no-scan

--auto-alias can offer short names after a successful scan. Browse needs a local Reticulum stack and the rns Python package for live listen.

items.title: Discover step by step
items.text:
Listen and store heard nodes:

pip-rns discover --seconds 60 --save
pip-rns discover ls

Scan stored nodes for packages (Nomad catalog when enabled, common packages index repos, release wheel checks):

pip-rns discover --save --scan
# or later
pip-rns discover scan
pip-rns discover packages

Clear stored discovery data when it goes stale:

pip-rns discover clear

Heard destination hashes can be used as rns://DESTINATION_HASH/group/repo when you know the path.

items.title: Search
items.text:
Search across aliases, indexes, and discovery:

pip-rns search lxm
pip-rns search reticulum

Then install by the short name that matched:

pip-rns install lxmfy

items.title: Aliases
items.text:
Save long remotes under short names:

pip-rns alias add lxmfy 06a54b505bb67b25ef3f8097e8001edc/public/LXMFy
pip-rns alias ls
pip-rns alias set lxmfy rns://identity/group/LXMFy
pip-rns alias rm lxmfy

Storage: ~/.config/pip-rns/aliases (or under PIP_RNS_CONFIG / --config).

Example file format:

lxmfy=06a54b505bb67b25ef3f8097e8001edc/public/LXMFy

items.title: Indexes (opt-in)
items.text:
An index is an rngit repo with a packages listing. Register only remotes you trust:

pip-rns index add rns://identity/group/index
pip-rns index sync
pip-rns index ls
pip-rns index list
pip-rns index search lxmfy
pip-rns index rm rns://identity/group/index

After sync, short names from that index resolve like aliases (aliases still win first).

items.title: Interactive install help
items.text:
With no arguments on a TTY:

pip-rns install

You get interactive help and a package picker when discovery or aliases have candidates.

items.title: Cost awareness
items.text:
Full source clones over RNS are expensive. Prefer:

  • release wheels (--from-release / auto when a release exists)
  • exported local wheels
  • cached source trees on repeat installs

pip-rns warns and confirms before the first expensive pull when it can.

items.title: Related
items.text:
• Install flags and backends: pip-rns
  • Publisher pins: trust

items.title: Getting started
items.text: pip-rns installs Python packages from Reticulum remotes you choose. opip packs and installs offline wheel bundles for USB or air-gap machines. Both ship in one package.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• Python 3.10 or newer (or a kit built with --with-runtime)
  • For mesh install and discover: a working Reticulum stack and the rns package
  • For rngit remotes: rngit on your PATH
  • An install backend helps (pip, pipx, uv, or poetry) but is not required

Without pip, use zipapps, --backend manual, or self-install. opip itself uses only the Python standard library.

items.title: Bootstrap without pip
items.text:
From a browser-downloaded wheel (Tor-friendly, no pip):

python3 get-opip.py --from-wheel pip_rns-*.whl -o .
python3 opip.pyz help airgap

Or from a release / make pyz:

python3 opip.pyz --version
python3 pip-rns.pyz doctor
python3 pip-rns.pyz self-install --user

Or from a source checkout:

PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m opip --version
PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pip_rns --version

items.title: Install pip-rns
items.text:
From a local wheel:

pip install pip_rns-*.whl
# or without pip:
python3 opip.pyz self-install --user

From source over rngit:

git clone rns://06a54b505bb67b25ef3f8097e8001edc/public/pip-rns
cd pip-rns
make
make install

Optional HTTPS bridges when you need them:

pip install pip-rns
# or
pipx install pip-rns
# or
pip install git+https://github.com/Quad4-Software/pip-rns

Check that the CLIs are on your PATH:

pip-rns --version
opip --version
pipx-rns --version

items.title: First useful checks
items.text:
Run doctor before you rely on the mesh:

pip-rns doctor
opip doctor

Add --fix if something looks wrong and you want repair hints:

pip-rns doctor --fix

Optional live check against a remote:

pip-rns doctor --online --remote rns://identity/group/repo

items.title: Shell completions
items.text:
pip-rns completion install
opip completion install

Pick a shell if detection is wrong:

pip-rns completion install --shell zsh

items.title: Offline first
items.text:
On a machine with network access, build a bundle, then move the file:

opip create -r requirements.txt -o ./pkg.opip

Copy pkg.opip to the target host, then:

opip verify ./pkg.opip
opip install ./pkg.opip

items.title: Mesh install by short name
items.text:
Listen, scan, and install in one flow:

pip-rns browse --install

Or install a name you already know:

pip-rns install lxmfy

items.title: Direct remote
items.text:
pip-rns install rns://identity/group/repo
# pin a release
pip-rns install rns://identity/group/repo@v1.0.0

On a TTY with no mode flags, pip-rns offers a menu. Latest release is preferred. A full source clone is labeled as expensive.

items.title: Source preference (cheapest first)
items.text:
1. Local .opip or exported .whl (no RNS needed)
  2. Signed release wheel over RNS
  3. Source clone over RNS (cached after the first pull)
  4. Opt-in indexes you register yourself

There is no default vendor index. Add only remotes and indexes you trust.

items.title: Where next
items.text:
• Day-to-day remotes and backends: pip-rns
  • Bundles and air-gap installs: opip
  • Publishers and verification: trust

items.title: opip
items.text:
opip builds integrity-backed offline wheel bundles (.opip) and installs them on machines that may never touch the public internet.

A bundle holds wheels, a pinned requirements list, and metadata used for verify and provenance checks.

items.title: What is inside a bundle
items.text:
Typical contents:

  • manifest.json - what the bundle claims to be
  • integrity.json - hashes for the packed files
  • lock.json - resolved pins (opip-lock/1)
  • sbom.json - CycloneDX 1.5 SBOM
  • optional publisher.json
  • wheels/ plus pinned requirements.txt
  • optional .rsg sidecar (Reticulum signature)
  • optional .rsm when published via rngit release

items.title: Create
items.text:
From the current project (reads pyproject.toml, setup.py, requirements.txt, or a lockfile):

opip create

From an explicit requirements file:

opip create -r requirements.txt -o ./pkg.opip

From a lockfile as source of truth (no live version resolution):

opip create --lockfile uv.lock -o ./pkg.opip
opip create --lockfile poetry.lock
opip create --lockfile requirements.lock

Pass --no-lock to ignore an auto-detected lockfile.

Target a Python and platform:

opip create -r requirements.txt --python 3.12 --platform win_amd64

One file for Windows, Linux, and macOS:

opip create -r requirements.txt --python 3.12 --platform universal

Private index or mirror (Warehouse JSON API):

opip create -r requirements.txt --index-url https://pypi.example/pypi

Air-gap create from a local wheel directory (no network):

opip create -r requirements.txt --find-links /media/usb/wheels --offline

items.title: Sign while creating
items.text:
opip keygen -o publisher.rns
opip create -r requirements.txt \
  --publisher "My Team" \
  --identity publisher.rns \
  --require-pypi-hash

Publish as an rngit release (creates an .rsm alongside):

rngit release -i publisher.rns rns://identity/group/repo create v1.0.0:./dist

items.title: Verify
items.text:
Always verify before install when the file came from elsewhere:

opip verify ./pkg.opip
opip verify ./pkg.opip --signer e46112d44649266d71fe2193e00a4710
opip verify ./pkg.opip --require-signature

A present .rsg is checked via the embedded pubkey. Pass --signer to pin the identity you expect. When --signer is unset, opip uses the shared pip-rns trust store (default or per-remote pin).

items.title: CI / automation
items.text:
opip --no-interactive -y verify ./pkg.opip --require-signature --signer IDENTITY
opip --json verify ./pkg.opip --require-signature
opip --quiet install ./pkg.opip --venv .venv -y

Also set CI=1 or OPIP_NO_INTERACTIVE=1, or run on a non-TTY. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 failure, 2 usage.

--json works on verify, info, list, and trust ls. --quiet / -q suppresses success stdout.

items.title: Install
items.text:
From a local file:

opip install ./pkg.opip

Into a venv:

opip install ./pkg.opip --venv .venv

With uv instead of pip:

opip install ./pkg.opip --venv .venv --backend uv

Default backend is pip. If a venv has no pip and uv is on PATH, install falls back to uv.

opip install ./pkg.opip --backend manual
opip install ./pkg.opip --user --break-system-packages

items.title: Kit and zipapps
items.text:
make pyz
python3 dist/opip.pyz help airgap
opip kit create nomadnet -o /media/usb --with-runtime --as-app \
  --proxy socks5h://127.0.0.1:9050
opip kit verify /media/usb
python3 opip.pyz self-install --user

Into a specific directory:

opip install ./pkg.opip --target /opt/wheels
opip install ./pkg.opip --target /opt/wheels --remember-target

User site (automatically adds --break-system-packages when PEP 668 blocks --user):

opip install ./pkg.opip --user

From Reticulum (release or path inside a release):

opip install rns://identity/group/repo@v1.0.0
opip install rns://identity/group/repo@v1.0.0:my-bundle.opip

HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, and git sources are also accepted when you need a bridge.

On PEP 668 protected interpreters, install can prompt for a venv, --user, or --target recovery path. The bundle Python version must match the current interpreter. An existing venv with the wrong Python is refused or recreated after confirmation.

items.title: Hand-off for other package managers
items.text:
.opip is not a pip/uv/poetry format. Extract wheels first:

opip extract ./pkg.opip -o ./wheelhouse --require-signature
pip install --no-index --find-links ./wheelhouse -r ./wheelhouse/requirements.txt

Optional PEP 503 simple index layout:

opip extract ./pkg.opip -o ./wheelhouse --simple-index
pip install --no-index --index-url file://$PWD/wheelhouse package-name

items.title: Export for USB
items.text:
opip export ./pkg.opip -o /media/usb/pkg.opip

Export verifies before copying.

items.title: Delta packs (scarce updates)
items.text:
Ship only changed wheels after the base bundle is already on the far side:

opip delta ./pkg-v1.opip ./pkg-v2.opip -o ./pkg-v1-to-v2.opipd
opip apply ./pkg-v1.opip ./pkg-v1-to-v2.opipd -o ./pkg-v2.opip

Apply fails closed if the base file hash does not match the delta.

items.title: Trust store
items.text:
Same store as pip-rns (~/.config/pip-rns/trust.json):

opip trust add default e46112d44649266d71fe2193e00a4710
opip trust ls
opip trust rm default

items.title: Manage registered bundles
items.text:
opip list
opip list installed
opip info ./pkg.opip
opip --json info ./pkg.opip
opip update nomadnet
opip update nomadnet --venv .venv
opip update nomadnet --no-reinstall -o ./nomadnet-new.opip
opip update nomadnet --emit-delta ./nomadnet.patch.opipd
opip uninstall nomadnet

opip update rebuilds from pinned requirements, reuses unchanged wheels from the previous bundle when hashes match, then reinstalls with upgrade/force-reinstall into the previous destination when known. Pass --identity to re-sign if the old bundle was signed.

Remembered destinations:

opip dest list
opip dest set my-bundle /opt/wheels
opip dest forget my-bundle

items.title: Windows helpers
items.text:
opip register-windows

Registers the .opip file association and Explorer context menus. Double-click uses the interactive open flow.

items.title: Doctor and help
items.text:
opip doctor
opip help
opip help create
opip help -i

items.title: Environment
items.text:
OPIP_DATA_DIR       state directory (same as --data-dir)
OPIP_JOBS           parallel downloads for create
OPIP_PYTHON         default --python
OPIP_PLATFORM       default --platform
OPIP_PUBLISHER      default --publisher
OPIP_IDENTITY       default identity path for signing
OPIP_SIGNER         default --signer for verify and install
OPIP_INDEX_URL      Warehouse JSON index base for create
OPIP_FIND_LINKS     local wheel directory for create
OPIP_OFFLINE        refuse network during create when set
OPIP_BACKEND        install backend: pip or uv
OPIP_COLOR          auto, always, or never
OPIP_NO_INTERACTIVE disable prompts
PIP_RNS_CONFIG      aliases and shared trust store

Global flags include --data-dir, --config, --no-color, --no-interactive / -y, --json, --quiet / -q, and --version.

items.text:

  • Signer pins and fail-closed rules: trust

items.title: pip-rns
items.text:
pip-rns resolves a remote (or alias, index name, discovery hit, or local wheel), then hands the artifact to pip, pipx, uv, or poetry.

pipx-rns is the same flow with pipx as the default backend, plus inject.

items.title: Install shapes
items.text:
Bare remote (install is implied):

pip-rns rns://identity/group/repo

Explicit install with a tag:

pip-rns install rns://identity/group/repo --ref v1.0.0
# same idea
pipx-rns install identity/group/repo@v1.0.0

Prefer a release wheel (no build step):

pip-rns install --from-release rns://identity/group/repo --ref v1.0.0

Force a source clone:

pip-rns install --from-source rns://identity/group/repo
# short form
pip-rns install -s rns://identity/group/repo

Require a release wheel or fail:

pip-rns install --require-release rns://identity/group/repo --ref v1.0.0

Branch-like refs such as @master or @main clone from source automatically.

items.title: Local wheels
items.text:
After pip-rns export or a USB mirror:

pip-rns install /media/usb/pkg-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl
pip-rns install /media/usb/mirror

items.title: Backends
items.text:
Default is pip. Switch with a flag:

pip-rns install --pipx identity/group/repo
pip-rns install --uv identity/group/repo
pip-rns install --poetry identity/group/repo

Or use the pipx entry point:

pipx-rns install identity/group/repo
pipx-rns inject my-app identity/group/repo

Flags after -- go to the backend:

pip-rns install identity/group/repo -- --break-system-packages
pip-rns install --poetry identity/group/repo -- --dev
pipx-rns install identity/group/repo -- --force

items.title: Releases
items.text:
List and inspect:

pip-rns release list rns://identity/group/repo
pip-rns release view rns://identity/group/repo v1.0.0

Export wheels for USB:

pip-rns export rns://identity/group/repo --ref v1.0.0 -o /media/usb/mirror

Signed releases fail closed unless verification succeeds. Pass --insecure only when you knowingly skip that check. See trust.

items.title: Offline and cache
items.text:
Use cache and local paths only (no RNS fetch):

pip-rns install --offline rns://identity/group/repo

RNS source installs reuse ~/.local/share/pip-rns/cache when possible. Set PIP_RNS_NO_CACHE=1 to force a fresh temp clone.

Editable checkout:

pip-rns install --editable rns://identity/group/repo

items.title: Destinations and venvs
items.text:
pip-rns install identity/group/repo --venv /path/to/venv --remember-venv
pip-rns venv list
pip-rns venv set default /path/to/venv
pip-rns venv forget default

items.title: Update, list, uninstall
items.text:
pip-rns update rns://identity/group/repo
pip-rns update rns://identity/group/repo --from-release --ref v1.2.0
pip-rns update rns://identity/group/repo --venv .venv
pip-rns list
pip-rns uninstall some-package

pip-rns update is a fresh reinstall from the remote (same options as install). Prefer --from-release when a wheel exists.

Add --pipx, --uv, or --poetry when the install used that backend.

items.title: Bundles via pip-rns
items.text:
pip-rns bundle install lxmfy-bundle@v1.0.0 --signer e46112d44649266d71fe2193e00a4710
pip-rns bundle verify ./my-bundle.opip --require-signature

items.title: Non-interactive / CI
items.text:
pip-rns --no-interactive install rns://identity/group/repo --from-release --ref v1.0.0 -y

Or set PIP_RNS_NO_INTERACTIVE=1 or CI=1.

items.title: Environment
items.text:
PIP_RNS_PIP             pip command (default pip)
PIP_RNS_PIPX            pipx command
PIP_RNS_UV              uv command
PIP_RNS_POETRY          poetry command
PIP_RNS_CONFIG          config directory for aliases and trust
PIP_RNS_USE_CACHE       set to 1 to enable cache
PIP_RNS_COLOR           auto, always, or never
PIP_RNS_NO_INTERACTIVE  disable prompts
NO_COLOR / FORCE_COLOR  standard color controls

Config lives under ~/.config/pip-rns/ (or %APPDATA%/pip-rns on Windows).

items.title: Command map
items.text:
pip-rns [install] <remote> [options]
pip-rns browse | search | discover | export | trust | alias | index
pip-rns release | venv | bundle | doctor | completion | help | update
pip-rns list | uninstall

For short names, aliases, and indexes, see discovery.

items.title: Sneakernet
items.text: Move packages without live RNS or HTTPS on the destination. Build or export on a connected machine, copy media, verify, then install.

items.title: Connected machine
items.text:
cd /path/to/project
opip create -o ./pkg.opip
# or
opip create -r requirements.txt -o ./pkg.opip --platform universal

Sign if you will require a signature on the far side:

opip create -r requirements.txt -o ./pkg.opip \
  --identity publisher.rns \
  --publisher "My Team"

Copy for transport:

opip export ./pkg.opip -o /media/usb/pkg.opip

items.title: Air-gap or USB target
items.text:
opip verify /media/usb/pkg.opip --require-signature
opip install /media/usb/pkg.opip

Pin the expected identity when you know it:

opip verify /media/usb/pkg.opip --signer e46112d44649266d71fe2193e00a4710 --require-signature
opip install /media/usb/pkg.opip --signer e46112d44649266d71fe2193e00a4710

items.title: Connected machine
items.text:
pip-rns export rns://identity/group/repo --ref v1.0.0 -o /media/usb/mirror

Optionally pin the publisher while exporting:

pip-rns export rns://identity/group/repo --ref v1.0.0 \
  --verify e46112d44649266d71fe2193e00a4710 \
  -o /media/usb/mirror

items.title: Target machine
items.text:
pip-rns install /media/usb/mirror/pkg-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl
# or point at the export directory
pip-rns install /media/usb/mirror

Offline mode refuses RNS fetches if something is missing:

pip-rns install --offline /media/usb/mirror/pkg-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl

items.title: Path C: signed bundle from an rngit release
items.text:
On the publisher side, create a signed .opip and attach it to a release. On the consumer:

opip install rns://identity/group/repo@v1.0.0
opip install rns://identity/group/repo@v1.0.0:my-bundle.opip

That path still needs RNS on the consumer. For true air-gap, copy the .opip file itself (Path A).

items.title: Path D: delta packs after the base is already there
items.text:
On the connected machine, after you already shipped pkg-v1.opip once:

opip create -r requirements.txt -o ./pkg-v2.opip
opip delta ./pkg-v1.opip ./pkg-v2.opip -o /media/usb/pkg-v1-to-v2.opipd

On the air-gap host that still has the base:

opip apply /media/usb/pkg-v1.opip /media/usb/pkg-v1-to-v2.opipd -o ./pkg-v2.opip
opip verify ./pkg-v2.opip --require-signature
opip install ./pkg-v2.opip

apply refuses a wrong base file (hash mismatch). Prefer this over copying a full universal bundle on every update.

items.title: Path E: USB kit (no Python / no pip)
items.text: Ship a ready-to-run stick: zipapps, integrity-backed .opip bundles, optional portable CPython, an AppImage-style Run launcher, and get-opip.py.

items.title: Zero prior tools (no pip online or offline, Tor, hand wheels)
items.text:
1. Download a pip_rns wheel and get-opip.py in the browser (Tor), or copy get-opip.py as a text file.
  2. Build zipapps from the wheel (no pip, no network):
python3 get-opip.py --from-wheel pip_rns-1.5.0-py3-none-any.whl -o .
  1. Build the kit from wheels you already saved:
python3 opip.pyz kit create nomadnet -o /media/usb \
  --find-links ./wheels --offline \
  --with-runtime --as-app

Or fetch over Tor instead of hand wheels:

python3 opip.pyz kit create nomadnet -o /media/usb \
  --with-runtime --as-app \
  --proxy socks5h://127.0.0.1:9050

items.title: Air-gap machine (AppImage-like)
items.text:
/media/usb/NomadNet
# or
/media/usb/Run

Optional classic venv install:

/media/usb/install.sh

Release zipapps alone:

make pyz
python3 dist/opip.pyz --version
python3 get-opip.py --from-dir dist -o ~/bin

items.title: Checklist
items.text:
1. Build or export on a machine you trust.
  2. Prefer signed artifacts (and signed zipapps when shipping kits).
  3. Copy the file, not a half-written download.
  4. Verify on the destination before install.
  5. Install into a venv or remembered --target when PEP 668 blocks system pip.
  6. Keep the publisher identity written down next to the media label.
  7. After the first full bundle, prefer .opipd deltas for scarce links.
  8. For hosts with no Python, use --with-runtime kits.

items.title: Mixing with aliases
items.text:
On the connected host you may resolve by short name. On the air-gap host, prefer the concrete file path unless you also copied config or use full remotes that already exist in cache.

# connected
pip-rns export lxmfy --ref v1.0.0 -o /media/usb/mirror
# air-gap
python3 pip-rns.pyz install /media/usb/mirror --offline

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text: Start with doctor. Fix what it reports before chasing mesh or signature issues.

items.title: Doctor
items.text:
pip-rns doctor
pip-rns doctor --fix
opip doctor

Online probe when remotes should be reachable:

pip-rns doctor --online --remote rns://identity/group/repo

items.title: PEP 668 (externally managed environment)
items.text:
System Python may refuse installs. opip and pip-rns can prompt for recovery when interactive:

  • create or use a virtualenv
  • install with --user when that is acceptable
  • install with --target into a directory you control

Non-interactive example with an explicit target:

opip install ./pkg.opip --target "$HOME/.local/opip-target"
pip-rns install ./pkg.whl --venv "$HOME/.venvs/app"

Remember destinations to avoid repeating the path:

opip install ./pkg.opip --target /opt/wheels --remember-target
pip-rns install pkg --venv /path/to/venv --remember-venv

items.title: Signature or trust failures
items.text:
Symptoms: install stops on a signed release or bundle.

Checks:

pip-rns trust ls
opip verify ./pkg.opip --require-signature
opip verify ./pkg.opip --signer YOUR_IDENTITY_HEX --require-signature

Fixes:

  • add the publisher with pip-rns trust add
  • pass --verify or --signer with the correct identity
  • confirm the .rsg sidecar traveled with the artifact
  • only then consider --insecure for a one-off debug install

items.title: Discovery hears nothing
items.text:
• Confirm Reticulum is up and the rns package imports
  • Widen the listen window:
pip-rns discover --seconds 120 --save
  • Nodes must announce git.repositories during that window
  • Discovery is passive. Silence usually means nobody announced nearby

Then scan:

pip-rns discover scan
pip-rns discover packages

items.title: Short name not found
items.text:
Resolution order is aliases, then indexes, then discovery packages.

pip-rns alias ls
pip-rns index sync
pip-rns index list
pip-rns discover packages
pip-rns search yourquery

Add an alias if you know the remote:

pip-rns alias add shortname identity/group/repo

items.title: Expensive clone / branch installs
items.text:
Branch refs clone source. Prefer a release when one exists:

pip-rns release list rns://identity/group/repo
pip-rns install --from-release rns://identity/group/repo --ref v1.0.0

Cache reuse lives under ~/.local/share/pip-rns/cache. Force a fresh clone with PIP_RNS_NO_CACHE=1 only when debugging.

items.title: Offline install misses artifacts
items.text:
--offline never contacts RNS. Export again on a connected host, or drop --offline if a fetch is acceptable.

pip-rns export rns://identity/group/repo --ref v1.0.0 -o ./mirror
pip-rns install --offline ./mirror

items.title: Completions or color oddities
items.text:
pip-rns completion install --shell zsh

Color settings:

PIP_RNS_COLOR=never
OPIP_COLOR=never
NO_COLOR=1
FORCE_COLOR=1

Classic Windows consoles stay colorless unless Windows Terminal / ConEmu / ANSICON or FORCE_COLOR is set.

items.title: Helpful exits
items.text:
• Ctrl-C and prompt cancel exit cleanly
  • Interactive command help:
pip-rns help -i
opip help -i
  • Root README for the compact command list

items.title: Still stuck
items.text:
1. Capture doctor output from both tools
  2. Note whether the path is release, source, local wheel, or .opip
  3. Note interactive vs CI (--no-interactive or CI=1)
  4. Confirm the publisher identity you expect

Then re-read trust or sneakernet for the path you are on.

items.title: Trust and signing
items.text: Both tools prefer verified artifacts. Signed release wheels and signed .opip bundles fail closed when verification cannot be confirmed, unless you explicitly opt into insecure mode.

items.title: Mental model
items.text:
1. Prefer a release wheel or a signed bundle over a raw source clone.
  2. Pin publishers you rely on so installs do not ask every time.
  3. Use --insecure only when you understand you are skipping checks.
  4. On USB paths, verify before install.

items.title: pip-rns trust store
items.text:
Remember a publisher for a remote:

pip-rns trust add rns://identity/group/repo e46112d44649266d71fe2193e00a4710
pip-rns trust ls

One-off pin on install:

pip-rns install --from-release rns://identity/group/repo \
  --ref v1.0.0 \
  --verify e46112d44649266d71fe2193e00a4710

Default identity when a remote has no stored pin:

pip-rns trust set-default e46112d44649266d71fe2193e00a4710
pip-rns trust forget-default
pip-rns trust rm rns://identity/group/repo

Store path: ~/.config/pip-rns/trust.json (or under PIP_RNS_CONFIG).

When --verify is omitted, pip-rns uses the trust store unless --insecure is set.

items.title: Unpinned remotes
items.text: On a TTY, an unpinned remote can prompt you to trust and remember the publisher. In CI or with --no-interactive, pass --verify, rely on a stored pin, or use --insecure deliberately.

items.title: Release signatures
items.text:
rngit release artifacts may include .rsg sidecars (and .rsm manifests). Signed releases must verify. If verification fails or cannot run, the install stops.

Skip only when you mean it:

pip-rns install --from-release rns://identity/group/repo --ref v1.0.0 --insecure

Manual check with rnid for a published wheel signature:

rnid -i e46112d44649266d71fe2193e00a4710 -V pip_rns-*.rsg

items.title: opip signatures
items.text:
Generate an identity and sign at create time:

opip keygen -o publisher.rns
opip create -r requirements.txt --identity publisher.rns --publisher "My Team"

Verify with a required signer:

opip verify ./pkg.opip --signer e46112d44649266d71fe2193e00a4710 --require-signature
opip install ./pkg.opip --signer e46112d44649266d71fe2193e00a4710

opip uses the same trust store as pip-rns. When --signer is omitted, verify and install resolve a pin from trust.json (per-remote, then default):

opip trust add default e46112d44649266d71fe2193e00a4710
opip trust ls
opip verify ./pkg.opip --require-signature

Environment defaults:

  • OPIP_IDENTITY for create
  • OPIP_SIGNER for verify and install
  • PIP_RNS_CONFIG for the shared trust store directory

items.title: Bundles through pip-rns
items.text:
pip-rns bundle verify ./pkg.opip --require-signature
pip-rns bundle install ./pkg.opip --signer e46112d44649266d71fe2193e00a4710

items.title: Practical habits
items.text:
• Treat --insecure as temporary and local, not a default in scripts.
  • Prefer --require-release or --from-release when a project publishes wheels.
  • Prefer --require-signature on air-gap machines after USB copy.
  • Keep publisher identities in the trust store or in deployment docs next to the remote URL.

Next: move verified artifacts offline in sneakernet.
